entries.translation: Nagaa / Naga, naga! Fayaketi! / Baga nagaan dhufte
entries.context: Borana / Oromo traditional greeting ('Peace, peace! Thy health!' — Tutschek 1845, p. 88, Aga's Letter)

entries.english: How are you? (Do you have peace?)
entries.translation: Nagaa qabdaa? / Akkam jirta? / Ati faya cabte?
entries.context: Borana / Oromo greeting & Tutschek (1845, p. 88)
Borana / Oromo response

entries.english: Good morning (Did you spend the night in peace?)
entries.translation: Bulte nagaa? / Akkam bulte? / Naga ambulte! (Krapf 1842)
entries.context: Borana / Oromo morning greeting (Krapf 1842, p. 16: "naga ambulte" = Good morning!; cf. bula "pass the night", Tutschek 1845)

entries.english: Good afternoon / Hast thou passed this day in peace?
entries.translation: Oolte nagaa? / Akkam oolte? / Ati naga olte har'a?
entries.pronunciation: ool-te na-gaa / a-ti na-ga ol-te har-a
entries.context: Tutschek (1845, p. 88, Aga's Letter: 'Ati naga olte had'a?')
Tutschek (1845, p. 90, closing of Otshu Aga's Letter)

entries.english: Rest in peace until we meet again
entries.translation: Nagan hafi hama nu wal agaruti
entries.pronunciation: na-gan ha-fi ha-ma nu wal a-ga-ru-ti
entries.context: Tutschek (1845, p. 91, closing of Akafed'e Dalle's Letter)

entries.english: Thank you / May God do good to him
entries.translation: Galatoomi (sg.) / Galatoomaa (pl.) / Wacayon iza ha tolu
entries.context: Borana / Oromo gratitude & Tutschek (1845, p. 90)
Borana / Oromo welcome

entries.translation: Nagaatti / Wak' nagaia si kakennu! ("Farewell! May God give thee peace!") / Nagaia hafu tshedde
entries.context: Borana / Oromo farewell & Krapf (1842, pp. 13, 31: "wak' nagaia si kakennu", "nagaia hafu tshedde" = bid farewell, "feiuma tshedde / salamata tshedde" = greet)

entries.english: Yes (and answer to a call: O!)
entries.translation: Eeyyee / Ee (ee-djed'a = to say yes, affirm; o! = answer to a call)

entries.english: No / Not / It is not so
entries.context: Tutschek (1845, §§ 10, 175, p. 90: 'wau, akana miti')

entries.english: It shall be done! / Let it be so!
entries.context: Tutschek (1845, § 149, p. 44 — ready consent to a request)

entries.english: Come! / Come here! / Let us go!
entries.translation: Kod'u! (pl. Kod'a! / emph. Kod'uka!) / Benuka! (Benu / Bena!)

entries.context: Tutschek (1845, § 254, p. 82 — entreating particle mê)

entries.translation: inni, ini (he, acc. iza) / ishiin, iz'in (she, acc. ishii, iz'i)
maali? / mali? (mal, emph. maltu) / malif? (malifi, maf, mafi)

entries.english: How much? / How many? / Which of the two?
entries.translation: mêka? / kami? (emph. kamtu; izakamtu? = which of the two?)

entries.context: Tutschek (1845, pp. 89–90)

entries.english: Amen! / So be it! & Praise and glory be unto thee! (Tutschek 1844)
entries.translation: hofu! ('Amen!', response to prayer, p. 201) / hocuban zi ha gau! ('Praise and glory be unto thee!', p. 201) / maren! (response of villagers during rain-processions around the sacred wateza tree, p. 166)
entries.pronunciation: ho-fu / ho-cu-ban zi ha ga-u / ma-ren
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1844) 'Dictionary of the Galla Language', Part I, pp. 166, 201

entries.translation: rago rag! (exclamation calling upon someone to tell a story or fable raga, p. 152) / hibo hib! or hipo hip! (exclamation when proposing a riddle hibo, p. 198)
entries.pronunciation: ra-go rag / hi-bo hib / hi-po hip
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1844) 'Dictionary of the Galla Language', Part I, pp. 152, 198

entries.translation: t'wu — aki — t'wu — tili! ('spit out — may it be so — spit out — finish!', spoken while chewing and spitting out blades of tila grass to ratify a solemn promise, p. 91) / cote wal cabad'u (mogezani goñizaniti wali cabu = hooking the little fingers moge together to ratify a wager or promise, pp. 47, 66)
entries.pronunciation: t'wu a-ki t'wu ti-li / co-te wal ca-ba-d'u

entries.english: Rock-Salt Currency (Amole), Fractions & Maria Theresa Silver Dollar (Biri) in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: amole (piece of rock-salt 2 hands long, 1 hand broad, 2 fingers thick, serving as standard currency, p. 13): mogor / mogora (2 amole, p. 172), tchabnana (1/2 amole, p. 72), kurmana / karmana (1/4 amole, p. 40), gimaz'i (1/8 amole in Dict. p. 61; 3/4 in Grammar p. 62), gedele / gadale / fotoqe (1/12 amole in Dict. pp. 52, 60, 122; 1/8 in Grammar p. 62), zanaga / çarmama (broken amole bound together with bark, pp. 183, 188) / biri (silver & Austrian Maria Theresa dollar with shoulder-clasp & diadem dots and engraver initials S. F., worth 23 amole in Liban or 20 in Goma, p. 135)
entries.pronunciation: a-mo-le / mo-go-ra / tchab-na-na / kur-ma-na / gi-ma-shi / ge-de-le / bi-ri

obboleessa / oboleza (nom. obolezi, voc. ya ob!, pl. obola / oboloni)

entries.translation: ormo (sg., pl. orma = Galla/Oromo person & people: "kuni ormōda" = This is a Galla) / ilma namma (free man, vs. gebruma = servitude, gebrumada baie = become free, gerbitsha = male slave, gerbiti = female slave)
entries.context: Rev. J. L. Krapf & Rev. C. W. Isenberg (1842, pp. 15, 26, 32–33)

entries.english: King, War-Leader (Abadula), Lady, Counsellor, Physician & Priest (Krapf 1842)
entries.translation: moti (king, prince; moti angafa = commander; motuma = kingdom) / abadula (general, war-leader) / gofta (lord) & gifti (mistress, lady) / tshawa (counsellor; mari = counsel) / Abba korritsha (physician, lit. "father of medicine") / kaletsha (Galla priest, vs. kêsi sidāma = Christian priest, Iltshāma = Muslim) / oggēsa (wise/skilled person)
entries.pronunciation: mo-ti / a-ba-du-la / gif-ti / tsha-wa / ab-ba kor-rit-sha / ka-let-sha / og-gee-sa

entries.english: Adoption Rites (Gada Guda, Gada T'ina, Gubifad'a & Balfad'a) in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: gada (state of adoption, p. 53): gada guda (great/complete adoption with full inheritance rights) vs. gada t'ina (little/incomplete adoption) / gubifad'a (adopting a child when one already has biological children, p. 68) / balfad'a (solemn adoption ceremony in which relatives walk single-file waliti ananiti carrying green twigs of the sacred Meeça tree to deliver the adoptive child baldja to his new father, pp. 94, 131)
entries.pronunciation: ga-da gu-da / ga-da t'i-na / gu-bi-fa-d'a / bal-fa-d'a / bal-dja
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1844) 'Dictionary of the Galla Language', Part I, pp. 53, 68, 94, 131

entries.english: Nuptial Sacrifice (Déca), Nuptial Cow (Rako) & Bride-Price Marriage in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: déca / déqi (nuptial sacrificial animal prepared at a wedding, p. 98) / rako (cow prepared at the marriage ceremony whose blood seals the union, p. 152) / muzuro (newly married bride or bridegroom, p. 1) / birmad'u & zadjeda (secondary wives or royal concubines, pp. 136, 180)
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1844) 'Dictionary of the Galla Language', Part I, pp. 1, 98, 136, 152, 180

entries.english: Funeral Memorial Staff (Ule Dimtu) & Mourning Scratches (Hofola) in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: ule dimtu ('red staff', wooden staff used to measure the length of a deceased relative's body and preserved in the house as a sacred memorial, p. 26) / hofola (mourning scratches made on the cheeks and temples with thorns or fingernails when lamenting the dead, p. 201) / awala (grave, burial mound, p. 7)
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1844) 'Dictionary of the Galla Language', Part I, pp. 7, 26, 201

entries.english: Times of Day, Relative Days & Seasons (Krapf 1842)
entries.translation: diruma & ganama (daybreak, early morning; borun dimate = dawn; urtshi ganama = morning-star) / safaia (noon, afternoon; safaia dura = forenoon) / wari dertu (midnight) / arda (to-day), borumti (following day), iftān (day after to-morrow), kallēsa (yesterday), dengādda (day before yesterday) / yogga (year; berdingata = last year; berekan = year before last) / bonna (summer, dry season) vs. ganā (winter, rainy season)
entries.pronunciation: di-ru-ma / sa-fa-ia / wa-ri der-tu / if-taan / den-gaad-da / bon-na / ga-naa

entries.english: Seven Days of the Week, Four Seasons, Lunar Months & 5-Year Sequence (Tutschek 1844)
entries.translation: 7 Days (torbanⁱ = week, p. 87; kurna = 10-day period, p. 38): 1. Gifti ('The Lady') or Kamiza (p. 60), 2. Djimada / Djimata (p. 80), 3. Zambata t'ina (preceded by cadame, pp. 40, 183), 4. Zambata guda (p. 183), 5. Zaño (p. 183), 6. Maczaño or Tafno (pp. 85, 161), 7. Arbi (p. 11) / 4 Seasons: birra (spring, ushered in mid-September when the yellow kelo flower blooms and celebrated with the Magzala / Maczala New Year feast on the duba hearth, pp. 34, 103, 114, 130, 135, 162), bona (summer, p. 139), arfaza (autumn/harvest, p. 11), ganna (winter/rainy season, p. 60) / Months: 1st hadoleza or hadami (p. 190 & Pt. II p. 75), 2nd hagayo (p. 189), 3rd wadabadji (p. 147), furma (p. 124) / 5-Year Relative Sequence (p. 131): barrakan (2 years ago) → barrengata (last year) → barrana (this year) → barragere (next year) → barratchanu (in 2 years)
entries.pronunciation: gif-ti, dji-ma-ta, zam-ba-ta t'i-na, zam-ba-ta gu-da, za-nyo, mac-za-nyo, ar-bi / bir-ra, bo-na, ar-fa-za, gan-na

entries.english: Divisions of the Day & Night in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: ganama aboro (very early dawn, p. 7) → ganama (sunrise to 8 a.m., p. 59) → dirama (8 to 10 a.m., p. 100) → ware (9 to 10 a.m., p. 148) → ware korate (forenoon before noon, p. 148) → oba / adun guba keza (noon, when calves are watered oba dyabi; afternoon hours counted oba lamuti, oba zaditi, oba afuriti, oba z'aniti, p. 23) → galgala (evening, p. 59) → wari (first night-watch, p. 148) → galgala dimemeza (midnight, p. 101)
entries.pronunciation: ga-na-ma a-bo-ro / di-ra-ma / wa-re / o-ba / gal-ga-la di-me-me-za
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1844) 'Dictionary of the Galla Language', Part I, pp. 7, 23, 59, 100–101, 138, 148

entries.english: Complete Cattle Classification under Lon (Loni) in Tutschek (1844, p. 160 & Pt. II p. 20)
entries.translation: Male cattle: tshabi (newborn calf) → djibitcha (young bull-calf) → gorba (3-year-old steer) → wofana (young bullock) → godiyo (pl. godiyoni, gelded plough-ox) → korma (pl. koromi, breeding bull: korma bordeda with erect hump vs. korma gurra with hanging hump, p. 36) → ulfin → zanga (castrated fattened ox) / Female cattle: tshabi (calf) → rad'a / rada (2-year-old heifer) → goromza (breeding heifer) → zã / zawa (cow; zilga = pregnant/milk cow giving colostrum zilga; gua = weaned calf or cow dried up of milk) → dulatcha (aged cow destined for ceremonial offering)
entries.pronunciation: tsha-bi, dji-bit-cha, gor-ba, wo-fa-na, go-di-yo, kor-ma, ul-fin, zan-ga / ra-d'a, go-rom-za, za-wa, zil-ga, du-lat-cha
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1844–1845) 'Dictionary of the Galla Language', Part I, pp. 36, 160; Part II, p. 20

entries.english: Sun (Biftu vs. Adu), Rainbow (Scarf of Heaven) & Locust (Horse of God) in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: biftu (the benign, life-giving sun, invoked as 'Wacayo biftun cara zodoma' = 'God thou sun with thirty rays', pp. 44, 134) vs. adu (the scorching, burning sun, p. 5) / zabata Wacayo, bidu & bidigira (rainbow, lit. 'girdle/scarf of Heaven', pp. 134, 181) / farda Wacayo (locust, lit. 'horse of God', p. 119)
entries.pronunciation: bif-tu / a-du / za-ba-ta wa-ca-yo / bi-di-gi-ra / far-da wa-ca-yo

dhaabachuu / d'âba (place, set up) / idyara (II idyarad'a = build a house)
jiraachuu / dyira (be, exist; II dyirad'a = live; invariant copula: -d'a)
du'uu / dua (2s duta, III duziza = cause to die) / ajjeesuu / adjeza (kill; cala = ceremonial offering/offer sacrifice; gorâ = ceremonial offering) / awala (bury; subst. tomb)

god'a (make, do; III goziza = let make, V goziziza = permit to be done) / uma (form, create; III umziza)

entries.english: Prayer 1 (Akafed'e's Prayer after the War of Hambo and Hamaya, 1845)
entries.translation: Wacayo laftana, goftako! ati na guba teza, ani zi dyalan taa. Ho haman nati d'ufe, aka mukni adu narra cabu, ati hama nati cabi, goftako, gadiza na tai! Wacayo, goftako, biftun cara zodoma, ho dini d'ufe ramoke lafati hin adjezizin, ira cabi!
entries.pronunciation: wa-ca-yo laf-ta-na gof-ta-ko a-ti na gu-ba te-za
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1845, pp. 84–87, Prayer 1 vv. 1–16 — 'Good God of this earth, my Lord! Thou art above me, I am below thee... be thou my shadow! Thou Sun with thirty rays...')

entries.translation: Ya Waca nagan na bultshite nagan na oltshi. Ede inand'aca karakora kan naga naf god'te, ya Waca, milkiko na gadyêlzi... zi wamad'etan ola, gofta goftan cabne.
entries.pronunciation: ya wa-ca na-gan na bul-tshi-te na-gan na ol-tshi
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1845, pp. 87–88, Morning Prayer — 'O God, thou hast let me pass the night in peace, let me pass the day in peace... lead my steps... O Lord, who hast no Lord!')

entries.translation: Ya Waca nagan na oltshite, nagan na bultshi, gofta goftan cabne; zi male dyaban hindyiru, tokitchi gidin cabne. Harkake dyaladan ola, harkake dyaladan bula, had'ikozi, abankozi.
entries.pronunciation: ya wa-ca na-gan na ol-tshi-te na-gan na bul-tshi
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1845, p. 88, Evening Prayer — 'O God, thou hast let me pass the day in peace, let me pass the night in peace... Under thy hand I pass the day, under thy hand I pass the night, thou art my mother, thou my father.')

May 17, 1841, aged ~22), Otshu Aga (from Urgeza in Sibu, who also transmitted songs from Bilile / Mahbuba of Guma, d. Oct. 27, 1840), and Aman Gonda (from Hibi in Goma, belonging to the wadjo / watcho subdivision of the Boranna sect, son of an aba fuño judicial officer) / Autonyms: oromo (pl. oromoni, p. 24) & himata ('orthodox believer', contrasted with faqi [Falasha], wada, zidama [Christian], and awalini [Muslim], p. 200) / Sects: Boranna (subdivision wadjo, p. 147) vs. djarzo (p. 78)

entries.english: The Five Galla Tribes / Gadaa Circumcision Rank Orders in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: 1st: horad'a ('the first tribe of the Gallas respecting their rank to the circumcision', p. 203) → 2nd: midjile ('the second tribe of the Gallas respecting the order which is observed amongst them at circumcision', p. 169) → 3rd: robale ('the 3d tribe of the Gallas respecting their claim to circumcision', p. 155) → 4th: kilole ('the name of the fourth tribe of the Gallas who have their claim to the order of the circumcision therefrom', p. 34) → 5th: dulo ('the fifth tribe of the Gallas respecting their rank to the circumcision', p. 104); plus djara (surgical circumcision feast held two years after the Gada / Buta festival, p. 78) and tchala (priests officiating at circumcision, p. 73)
entries.pronunciation: ho-ra-d'a, mi-dji-le, ro-ba-le, ki-lo-le, du-lo / dja-ra / tcha-la

entries.english: Political, Judicial & Military Hierarchy in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: moti (king, fem. meti, p. 171; royal palace = mazara, p. 167; royal household = zadjeda / birmad'u, p. 180; royal groom leading war-steed farta lola or courser djolle = nao, p. 177) / zoreza, zalgana & momoti (princes, nobles, p. 184) / aba ganda (town governor chosen from the zoreza, pp. xxi, 6) / aba lafa (landed proprietor; settled tenants/vassals = gubziza, p. 68) / mangudo or bera (senate, court of aldermen & judges sitting at the gude dubi or yai dyidu assembly place, pp. 67, 84, 133, 144, 167) / aba fuño ('master of the cord', judicial & police officer under the aba ganda, pp. 6–7, 125) / cuge (sergeant/tipstaff under the aba fuño, p. 49) / cabi (distrainer for debt, p. 41) / erada (bailiff, p. 16) / gindo (wooden leg-stocks prison, p. 62) / findja Lali (waterfall in Hambo used for capital execution, p. 122) / guma (customary restitution for customary restitution or ransom for a captive, p. 71; gumad'a naga = women's peace offerings)

entries.english: Heroic Distinctions (Gondala vs. Gurgudu), Triumphal Song (Gerara) & Insignia in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: gondala (hero/champion who has slain an enemy, elephant, lion, rhino, or buffalo and earned the right to anoint his head with butter, p. 66, fixing the zariti asparagus-thorn in his hair during the gerara triumphal song so the melting butter does not fall, p. 182, wearing the ivory armlet ilbora, p. 20, round earring d'ugo, p. 116, gold/silver chain ear-pendant loti, p. 159, and military bracelet gudidja, p. 67, while leaving the kuba piece of skin-meat in the field for wild beasts, p. 38) vs. gurgudu (man who has not yet performed a heroic exploit, p. 69)

entries.english: Priesthood, Divination, Sacrificial Raven (Arageza), Sacred Trees & Folklore Beings in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: ayana (guardian spirit / soul) & ayanditcha / ayantu (dream-interpreting priest/priestess, p. 8) / calu, calitcha & caliti (high sacrificial priests and priestesses, p. 45) / mora ilalitcha (haruspex who divines the future by inspecting the veins of the sacrificial peritoneum fat mora, p. 172) / djila (magician/healer, p. 80) / arageza (white-necked sacrificial raven Corvus albicollis that consumes offerings on the wooden sacrificial fork muka haçi in place of God, pp. 9, 196) / Sacred trees: wateza (Bruce's Wanzey tree, Cordia abyssinica, p. 147), lafto (acacia, p. 157), meeça (Ilex/palm twig of adoption & oaths, p. 168), makaniza (Croton macrostachyus, p. 161), and ba (sacred tree in Sibu, p. 125) / Folklore beings: bulgu (male man-eating giant/ogre in fables, p. 143), bauda (female half-human cannibal ghost, p. 128), adi (white shape-shifting phantom, pp. 4–5), and buda (sorcerer/evil eye capable of turning into a hyena, p. 141)

entries.english: 15 Verbatim Galla Proverbs (Magmaga) in Tutschek's Dictionary (1844)
entries.translation: (1) 'afan agabudan kad'ad'u' ('Pray with an empty/fasting mouth', p. 3); (2) 'ati malⁱ bechta harka arabu male' ('What knowest thou but to lick off the hand?', p. 9); (3) 'yo argite ebizi, yo d'abte abari' ('When thou receivest, bless; when thou dost not receive, curse!', p. 16); (4) 'ilkanin namni gitᵃumtu fira' ('By the teeth all men are friends — i.e., do not trust every smiling face', pp. 20, 121); (5) 'idya Wacᵃ kaba ura' & 'hadarinza kaba ura' ('The eye of God penetrates the wall' & 'His wisdom penetrates a wall', pp. 27, 190); (6) 'uma Wacayoti hinkolfin' ('Do thou not laugh at any of God's works!', p. 28); (7) 'ini aka kozi tȧ' ('He is like dung — i.e., as good and useful as manure', p. 37); (8) 'yo canqen gaya keza ut'ale namni indua' ('When a spark jumps out of the pipe, someone dies', p. 45); (9) 'ini aka gararati bifaza didirad'a' ('He changes his colour like a chameleon', p. 56); (10) 'Tchaba ati murte Naman bad'z'izin; — Liqi ati fud'te Naman bazizin' ('The wood which thou didst hew, let nobody carry; — The loan which thou didst take, let nobody pay', p. 72); (11) 'tchitinif ibida waliṅ gain; biçanif ibidi wali ha gau' ('Chaff and fire shall not come near each other; water and fire may approach each other', p. 74); (12) 'mukni Wacᵃ careṅ domu' ('The edge of the spear of God is not blunted', p. 102); (13) 'ibidif biçan hirmiṅ cabu, fulif gongon d'okzaṅ cabu' ('Fire and water have no prohibition, face and throat have no concealment', p. 114); (14) 'ini aka falʿanati afan nama dyala d'abad'a' ('He stands like a spoon under the mouth of men', p. 120) & 'madirati hinkolfini' ('Do not laugh during dinner', p. 162); (15) 'hodjad'z'u wayo mo tau wai?' ('Is it better to work or to sit idle?', pp. 146, 201), 'bokeṅi mit'ileṅ adjezu, zi adjeza?' ('The rain kills not even a little ant, will it kill thee?', p. 170), 'handangon qilenza ufiti naqeti ilman god'ad'a?' ('Does the hen lay eggs impregnated by the air?', p. 177), & 'namni ho bola lit'e hadaroma' ('When a man has fallen into the pit, he becomes wise', p. 190)

entries.english: 7 Verbatim Galla Songs (Wetu) in Tutschek's Dictionary (1844)
entries.translation: (1) 'Koromin wal ate, Latshu gugurod'a; — Nadeṅ wal arate, Latshu muzurod'a' ('Bulls gore, both are black; — Women altercate, both recently married', p. 1); (2) 'Ombo z'an bared'a, Maf baretu d'abe? Dyalalti d'ukuba, Maf arera d'abe?' ('Ombo z'an is handsome, why does he not find a fair maiden? Love is an illness, why does it not find medicine [arera]?', p. 10); (3) 'Wanin korriza, Muka cabad'a; Diarzi roriza, Durba kad'ad'a' ('The Wanin monkey growls and grasps a tree; the foolish bald-pate fellow means to win a maiden's heart', p. 36); (4) 'Galani na ñad'e, Giben na gezize; — Ano d'ufa djenan, D'iben na tezize' ('The river devoured me and carried me to the lake; — I said I shall come, but an obstacle detained me', p. 61); (5) 'Gaya t'ut'uko, Tambo na d'abi, Fag'afuftuko, Yambo na wami!' ('My pipe-smoker, put the tobacco here; my flute-player, call the dancers!', pp. 117–118); (6) 'Cotani cotani yaa babazani; Djed'ani djed'ani gargar nu bazani' ('They ploughed, ploughed and made a trench; they chattered, chattered and separated us', p. 127); (7) 'Zila zimalan yaba, Zimali dameṅ cabu; — Zila gandaran gala, Gandatu wareṅ cabu' ('In vain I climb a reed, a reed has no branches; — In vain I return to town, the town has no feeling for glory', p. 148) & 'Lenzan lon guza Bia gubati; D'enzan lon buza Iya nafati' ('Lenza grass causes cattle to dry up on the mountain; flight exposes cattle to screams of desperation', p. 158)
entries.pronunciation: ko-ro-min wal a-te / om-bo shan ba-re-d'a / ga-la-ni na nya-d'e

entries.english: Dr. Krapf's (1850, pp. viii–ix, 1–64) Dana River (Tana) Kigalla Dialect vs. Shoan Galla & Origin of "Ormania"
entries.translation: Studied in 1845 from Tana River Galla (Orma / Southern Oromo) near Takaongo and Berrarata to compare with his 1842 Shoan Galla vocabulary (10–12 degrees north) • Autonym & "Ormania" (p. ix): Coins "Ormania" ("an African Germania") from the Galla autonym Orma ("men / brave people"), correcting a French writer who confused Orma with morma ("neck") • Shared Amharic-Galla roots proved genuinely Cushitic/Galla because the Dana Galla have no contact with Christian Abyssinia • Greetings & Blessings (pp. 20, 24): nagaia bulte? ("good morning / hast thou passed the night in peace?") & wakne nágaia si kennu! ("farewell! may God give thee peace!")
entries.pronunciation: or-ma / or-ma-ni-a / be-rra-ra-ta / na-ga-ia bul-te / wak-ne na-ga-ia si ke-nnu
entries.context: Rev. Dr. J. L. Krapf (1850) 'Vocabulary of Six East-African Languages' (Tübingen), Preface pp. viii–ix & pp. 20, 24

entries.english: Dana River Kigalla Governance, Law, Religion & Nature Lexicon (Krapf 1850, pp. 1–64)
entries.translation: Religion & Priesthood: Wāka (God; soda Wakáti = godliness, p. 23), moru / bersíftu (wise man / priest / teacher, pp. 38, 63), kallu (soothsaying/divination, p. 47), bitta (sacrifice; bitta balfatje = to offer sacrifice, p. 42), kákăno / kákata (oath/covenant, pp. 12, 34), tába & makmáksa (story, fable, proverb, pp. 19, 39, 49) • Governance & War: móti / heiu (king/governor; mótuma / heiyóma = kingdom, p. 29), murra heiuáti (vice-regent, p. 60), subbo / abba duláti (general/commander, p. 22), nama ka yákamsu (judge; yákama = law/judgement, pp. 29–30), nágaia & arára (peace/reconciliation; ka arársu = mediator/peacemaker, pp. 33, 36) • Geography & Trade: Máro (Galla name for the Dana/Tana River, p. vii; gélăna = river, melka = ford, pp. 21, 41), mánia (sea; mánia gudda = ocean, pp. 34, 43), hówolo / hirrino (ship/canoe, p. 44), tjábi dakatjáti (snow/hail on mountains, p. 46), ilka arbu (elephant tusk / ivory traded to Pokomo and Swahili, p. vii & p. 29)
entries.pronunciation: wa-ka / mo-ru / ber-sif-tu / ka-llu / bi-tta / mo-ti / hei-u / su-bbo / a-ra-ra / ma-ro / ge-la-na
